query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: seat_comfort_issue
per_column.rationale: A boolean flag for seat complaints extracted from review text; useful driver dimension for the query. Partially overlaps with the existing Seat Comfort rating but adds a text-derived issue signal. Samples align well (dreadful seats = True, comfortable = False).

per_column.name: food_quality_decline
per_column.rationale: Flags food-related negatives; relevant to satisfaction analysis. Somewhat redundant with Food & Beverages rating but captures a specific 'decline' narrative. Samples correctly False for positive food mentions.

per_column.name: service_inconsistency
per_column.rationale: Near 50/50 split gives good grouping leverage on a plausible recommendation driver. Sample with 'consistently good' correctly False; interpretation is a warranted reading of text.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Useful multi-level categorical for analysis. However 'responsive' appears assigned even where reviews say nothing about responsiveness (e.g. the seat-complaint review with no service mention was labeled 'responsive'), suggesting a default that overstates a silent source; a 'not stated' would be more grounded.

per_column.name: booking_operational_failure
per_column.rationale: Distinct operational failure axis not captured by original rating columns; genuinely useful for root-cause of non-recommendation. Samples with no booking issues correctly False.

per_column.name: inflight_entertainment_failure
per_column.rationale: Overlaps with existing Inflight Entertainment rating but adds a specific failure flag. Sample with dreadful headphones/sound correctly True; well grounded.

per_column.name: aircraft_age_condition
per_column.rationale: New physical-product axis relevant to comfort complaints. Interestingly the 'older aircraft ... good condition' sample is False, which is a defensible reading (age noted but condition fine). Grounded.

per_column.name: crew_service_attitude
per_column.rationale: Rich multi-level categorical, strong grouping value for service-driven recommendation analysis. Mostly grounded (warm_attentive for welcoming crew), but the seat-complaint review with no crew commentary was labeled 'neutral_efficient', an unwarranted specific where text is silent.

per_column.name: traveller_segment
per_column.rationale: Useful segmentation, but largely redundant with the original 'Type of Traveller' column. Groundedness is weakened: the 'gave my mom a bday cake' review labeled Solo_Leisure and the excellent-performance review labeled Family_Leisure appear to be unsupported specifics unless sourced from the existing column.

per_column.name: cabin_class
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with the existing 'Class' column, adding little new leverage. Grounding is questionable: the 'amazing flight' review labeled Business has no class cue in text, an unwarranted specific for a silent source.

judge.rationale: The added columns give several genuinely useful new analytical axes (operational failures, crew attitude, service inconsistency, entertainment/aircraft issues) that let the analyst decompose drivers of non-recommendation beyond the raw numeric ratings. A few columns (traveller_segment, cabin_class) largely duplicate existing original columns and add limited leverage. Groundedness is generally sound for extraction-style flags, but the multi-level categoricals (customer_service_responsiveness, crew_service_attitude) and the class/segment fields show a tendency to assign confident defaults where the source text is silent, which slightly lowers overall groundedness.
